$Comment: The introduction to the Disenchanting Table: the Adventurer's Guide, standing in the Forgotten
Temple, points the player at the priest standing beside Sawyer Marn. The quest exists to make
the player notice him. It has the same shape and the same minimal gate as the introductions
to Marn (Meet_The_Sawyer) and to the Mastery Trainer, so a player can meet the three in any
order once the temple meeting is behind them. Until it is taken Orrin has nothing of his own
to offer, so asking him for work sends the player to the guide (his conversation's vouch_first
screen).
Npc.ViewId names the guide's temple id, so the guide is who OFFERS it: it appears on their
quest list down in the temple, right after the meeting that brought the player there, and the
guide's temple screens carry a pointer line about the one with the book that takes it on.
Marn's conversation can also take it on, from his question about the priest next to him; a
quest is accepted wherever a conversation's Accept runs, and either way it is the same quest.
The step names the enchanter's role id, so the errand is taken from one character and
discharged at another. Orrin's placement authors no Identity.NpcId, so the character IS the
role, and any other standing of Mmo_Enchanter credits the step just as well.
TurnInAt names the enchanter, so the reward is collected where the errand ends rather than on
a walk back to the guide: the quest sits in the Claim bucket and waits in the log until the
player collects it from Orrin's own quest list. CompletionDialogue names Orrin's conversation,
so collecting the reward at him plays his next line, and with this introduction settled the
first job he can offer is The Lesser Table, so the player lands on the screen that hands it
over.
A talk step is credited by a MarkTalked beat inside the conversation, never by pressing F, so
Orrin's dialogue carries one on the line the player picks. Re-point the step and that beat has
to move with it.
The Enchanting experience is deliberately small: a nod toward the skill the whole table chain
trains, not a payout worth walking over for on its own. Requires.Quests names the jar's temple
meeting, which chains this pack onto the end of the starter run; without it collected the
guide has nothing to offer. The feature factor keeps the quest out of the log on a server with
the station engine switched off, where Orrin never appears at all. Listing.Hidden keeps it off
open listings until it is taken; a giver always lists its own quests, so the guide still
offers it in the temple.
Name: Meet_The_Enchanter
